title: How accurate were portolan charts?
excerpt: I read 248 places on the Carta Pisana and the Catalan Atlas and measured them against the real coast. Both charts are turned about 11 degrees off north, the Mediterranean is drawn to within a few dozen kilometres, and beyond Gibraltar they fall apart.
seo_description: The Carta Pisana and the Catalan Atlas measured against the real coast: a tilt of about 11 degrees, a superb Mediterranean and a shrunken Atlantic.
header_alt: Title card on parchment reading 'How accurate were portolan charts?' in black and red lettering, beside the ragged Carta Pisana with a red grid of the true meridians and parallels bent across it and coloured dots for the places read, and the line 248 places on two medieval sea charts, both turned about 11 degrees off true north.
